subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.
reasoning:
I'm designing a baku creature blending tapir body, elephant trunk, tiger paws, ox tail, and lion mane, rendered in ukiyo-e style with flat colors, indigo outlines, and cloud/wave patterns. Now I'm planning the joint hierarchy and body structure to build this efficiently.

Setting up hips, spine chain, and neck joints...

Defining the body sweep path...

Still working out leg geometry...

For feet I'll add small toe spheres with gold claw cones, and set the hip attachment points offset from the spine so legs sit naturally on either side. I'm also sketching a short tail chain with a tufted end and starting on the head structure.

Now I'm working out the head joint and skull sphere scaling, then building a curling trunk chain down from the snout with tapered sweep radius for the nostril tip, plus a lower jaw joint positioned just below and forward of the head.

Next I'm shaping the jaw with a small tapering frustum box mesh beneath the trunk base, adding rounded tapir ears with white rim trim, and placing ukiyo-e style kabuki eye decals—almond-shaped with red eyeliner outline and black iris—onto the sides of the skull for a bold, readable look.

Then I want to add a shishi-style curled mane along the neck using swirled flame-cloud tuft textures, plus small gold horns and baku-like tusks from the jaw, with a cloud emblem on the forehead and vermilion-gold karakusa spiral decals on the shoulders and haunches for extra ornamentation.

I settle on about five textures total — eye, flank swirl, mane tuft, tail tuft, and forehead cloud emblem — with no ground element, and pick a palette of indigo, cream, vermilion, gold, and ink tones. Writing body paint shader logic...

Paws get gold claws over indigo. For the legs I'm sweeping a chain shape with the dark coloring, and building the skull as a scaled sphere attached to the head bone, letting world axes handle the scaling since no orientation is specified.

Now I'm setting up the skull surface for decals and placing mirrored eye shapes using local offsets from the head bone, with a wide eye texture and a red liner detail at the outer corner.

Next I'm positioning the ears with an extruded oval outline, choosing orientation vectors so the plane faces outward and slightly forward, then adding a thicker cream rim extrusion around the edge.

Then I'm planning the mane: scattering tuft cards along the neck and upper body sweep, filtered by position and normal direction, and figuring out a gradient coloring for the fur texture.

Still placing mane and tail tufts...

For the tail tip I'll ring eight small cards at 95% along the sweep, angled back and down. Then I'm chaining the trunk as a parented sequence of segments off the head joint, using five catmull points for four spans, with a tapering sweep radius and cream-tipped gradient coloring.

I'm adding small dark spheres for nostrils near the trunk tip, and spiking tusks off the jaw with a base offset to each side.

Then I'm sweeping curved gold horns from the head top with tapering radius, and placing a glowing vermilion jewel sphere near the forehead at the skull's crown.

Now I'm adding decorative decals: a small cloud swirl on the skull, and karakusa swirl patterns on the flanks and shoulders rendered in vermilion and gold with ink outlines, positioned to sit against the body surface on both sides.

For the lower body, I'm sizing the belly and legs to connect smoothly to the hip joint, then building paw geometry for each foot -- small toe spheres and claw cones attached near the leg tip, with front and hind feet positioned along the z-axis and bound to their respective bone chains.

Now I'm setting up the limb kinematics: defining named joint chains (shoulder/elbow/wrist for front legs, hip/knee/ankle for hind legs) rooted at the spine or hips, with bend directions chosen so front legs flex backward and hind legs flex forward, keeping everything anchored near the body's y=0.95 line.

I'm building the spine and hips joint chain, then adding a tail made from a smooth curve through four points, tapering its radius and adding a tuft ring at the tip using the tangent direction rather than the surface normal. Then I move on to setting up the jaw joint.

Now I'm positioning the jaw relative to the head and building a frustum-shaped box for it between two computed head-local points, colored dark. I'm setting up thick red bushy brow sweeps above each eye using symmetric head-local offsets.

Checking placement against the skull ellipsoid to make sure brow and eye points land near the surface rather than inside, verifying with relative-coordinate sums close to 1.

Setting eye direction and size, then sketching the texture SVGs: an almond eye with sclera, gold iris and ink outline, a flame-shaped mane curl with vermilion-to-gold gradient, and a karakusa spiral swirl pattern in layered ink and vermilion strokes.

I'm now placing accent features on the head geometry: a cloud decal for the forehead and repositioning a glow sphere or jewel near the forehead front, working out the local offset coordinates so it sits correctly on the ellipsoid skull shape.

Still shaping the body path...

I'm checking the trunk's path points against the floor and overall head height to make sure proportions stay sensible with horns and mane included. Then I'm setting up the mane as scattered surface cards along the body sweep, filtering by position and normal direction to control where tufts appear, plus adding a sparser backline layer.

Now I'm planning the card texture coloring, deciding to leave the base color undefined since the texture itself carries the tint, and adding slight random variation per card. I'm sketching out the final imports needed—builder, frame, rng, spline and bezier helpers, limb and paint utilities, noise/mottle/scales/gradient, and glow from the kit—along with helper functions for blobs and paws, including toe spheres and claw spikes built from bone tips.

Finalizing the cards call with its size, lean, bend, flow, and vary parameters, I'm setting the head paint to the dark variant and skipping the cream cheek detail for simplicity, then writing out the meta export to wrap things up.
